page: Amazon Web Services t2.large is an entry-tier general-purpose instance featuring burstable CPU performance managed through a Xen hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. It provides 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions, with a 45 MB L3 cache. There are no attached GPUs or local storage drives, requiring external EBS volumes for persistence, and the network interface provides a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate that the legacy Broadwell architecture and burstable throttling model fall into the lower performance tiers. The instance achieved 879.89 in single-core and 1743.88 in multi-core stress-ng tests, ranking in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems. Geekbench scores reached 876.0 for single-core and 1571.0 for multi-core compute. Memory benchmarks show large-block uncached read speeds of 20.07 GB/sec and write speeds of 13.01 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 1.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.08 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. A modest exception is lightweight LLM text generation using a 135M model, where it delivered 78.0 tokens/sec, placing it within the middle 50 percent.

Due to its burstable allocation and lack of integrated storage, the t2.large is configured for budget-conscious scenarios rather than sustained compute density. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio accommodates basic background services, low-traffic staging environments, small test databases, and bursty development workloads that remain idle for long intervals to accumulate CPU credits.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.large is a general-purpose, burstable instance based on the Xen hypervisor and powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. It features 2 vCPUs (2 physical cores), 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, including Geekbench (876.0 single-core, 1571.0 multi-core) and PassMark tests, the instance typically ranks in the lower percentiles due to its older CPU architecture and burstable resource allocation. Memory bandwidth reaches 20.07 GB/sec on uncached reads. Given its hardware constraints, t2.large provides a low-cost profile best suited for lightweight web servers, development environments, and applications with intermittent CPU utilization.
